statement.p: Compute the flux of \vec F = 4 x\vec i + 4 y\vec j + z\vec k over the quarter cylinder S given by x^2+y^2=16, 0\leq x\leq 4, 0\leq y\leq 4, 0\leq z\leq 4, oriented outward.

static.solution:
\vec k-component of \vec F does not contribute to the flux as it is perpendicular to the surface. The vector field 4 x\vec i + 4 y\vec j is everywhere perpendicular to S and has constant magnitude ||(4 x)^2+(4 y)^2|| = 4 on the surface S. Thus \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A =\int_S 4(x\vec i +y\vec j)\cdot d\vec A =4\cdot \hbox{Area of }S = 4\frac{16 \pi}{2} = 32\,\pi.
Alternatively, the flux can be computed by integrating with respect to x and z, treating y as a function of x and z. A parameterization of S is given by y=\sqrt{16-x^2}, 0\leq x\leq 4, 0\leq y\leq 4, 0\leq z\leq 4. Thus, \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{4}\int_0^{4}(4 x\vec i + 4 \sqrt{1-x^2}\vec j+ z\vec k) \cdot(-y_x\vec i + \vec j- y_z \vec k)\,dx\,dz = \int_0^{4}\int_0^{4}(4 x\vec i+ 4 \sqrt{1-x^2}\vec j+ z\vec k) \cdot\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{16 -x^2}}\vec i +\vec j + 0\vec k\right)\,dx\,dz = \int_0^{4}\int_0^{4}\left(4\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{16-x^2}} + 4 \sqrt{16 -x^2}\right)\,dx\,dz = 4 \int_0^{4}\int_0^{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{16-x^2}}\,dx\,dz = 64\cdot \arcsin \frac{x}{4}\bigg|_0^{4} = 32\,\pi.
